content:
This is your sketch, not your statement — but even a sketch this rough tells me something worth acting on.

Your ≈€1,200/mo fixed base leaves ≈€1,500/mo free after income. The pot needs ≈€170/mo — that's ≈6% of take-home, and the free cash covers it without a fight. The real question is the ≈€1,120/mo of drift: money that isn't eating out, isn't saving, and isn't explained. You flagged that yourself as unsure, and you mentioned things have shifted since the rent went up — so some of that drift may be newer and stickier than it looks on paper.

The one move: set up a standing transfer of ≈€300/mo on payday. Sized at roughly half the drift, it shouldn't bite. At that pace the pot lands in ≈3 months instead of ≈10.

You called your ≈€48/mo of subscriptions a leak. A real month settles whether it's genuinely that, or just a few you'd forgotten you still use.

Checking a real month does two things. It swaps every ≈ for an actual number — estimate against reality, side by side. And the habits half of this picture is still empty: timing, what's recurring, where the drift actually lives. Estimates can't see any of that; only real transactions can. Right now, I know you about 56%. Checking a real month is what takes that past 70%.

[CTA:start_statement_check]Check my numbers[/CTA]

— C.
